alignments.note: The construct noun קְבֻצַת (a gathering of) is recast by the ASV as a finite comparative clause 'As they gather'. The supplied 'As' belongs to the noun whose adverbial function licenses it (rule 33), and the supplied subject pronoun stays inside the same rendering; head on 'gather', the word carrying the lexeme (rule 31). Competing reading: mark 'As' added under rule 55 as a supplied subordinator; rejected because no clause-level conjunction is being duplicated here — the comparison is the accusative noun's own force.
Nomen rectum of the construct chain, but the ASV's verbal recasting writes it as a bare object, so no 'of' is present to place (rule 19 read off the ASV).
Construct תּוֹךְ takes 'midst' with the supplied 'the': no article morpheme stands anywhere in this chain, so the construct noun takes a supplied 'the' under rule 29.
Nomen rectum takes the relational 'of' (rule 19); its own 'the' is likewise supplied, since כּוּר carries no article morpheme (rule 29), and the head is the noun in 'of + noun' (rule 24).
לְ before the infinitive construct, rendered by the English infinitival 'to'.
אֵשׁ is anarthrous; the supplied definite article belongs to the nominal expression it determines and is not added (rule 15).
לְ before the hiphil infinitive construct → the infinitival 'to'.
Hiphil infinitive נָתַךְ → melt. The following 'it' is not part of this unit: no object morpheme is present, so rule 44's supplied-object clause leaves it added.

The object pronoun of 'to melt it' answers to no morpheme — הַנְתִּיךְ carries no object suffix — so it is added under rules 30 and 44 rather than folded into the infinitive's unit. MACULA's gloss 'melt.[it]' brackets the pronoun precisely because it is not in the Hebrew (rule 39).
כֵּן → so, closing the comparison opened by 'As'.

The inflected verb takes its subject pronoun and auxiliary with the lexical verb, headed on the lexical predicate (rules 17, 24). The unit is discontinuous in English order only because the ASV inverts 'so will I'.

One אֶתְכֶם serves all three coordinated verbs in the Hebrew (gather, set down, melt), and the ASV writes 'you' with each; every occurrence belongs to the single suffix's one discontinuous unit (rules 18, 25), and none is added. Head taken on the first occurrence, as rule 55 heads a repeated realization on the first; heading on t048, the 'you' standing beside the verb the suffix is actually attached to, is the defensible alternative.
Waw of the consecutive form takes the connective 'and'; the verb takes the verb (rule 14).

Hiphil of נוח 'set down, deposit' → 'I will lay ... there', with the locative particle completing the verb's own rendering as a phrasal particle does under rule 44; the unit is discontinuous around the suffix's 'you' (rule 25) and heads on the lexical verb. Competing reading: treat 'there' as an ASV supply answering to no morpheme and mark it added under rule 30; I take the verb reading because הִנִּיחַ lexicalizes the depositing-in-a-place that 'lay ... there' renders, and the head is unaffected either way.
Waw of the consecutive form → and (rule 14).
Hiphil נָתַךְ → melt; the auxiliary 'will' of t042 is gapped over this coordinated verb in English and is written once, so nothing further is placed here.
Definite direct-object marker אֵת (H853): the ASV writes the object bare ('melt you'), spending no English word on the object relation itself, so the marker is its own unrepresented unit (rule 16).

review_notes: Both 'the's in 'the midst of the furnace' are supplied: neither תּוֹךְ nor כּוּר carries an article morpheme, so rule 29's supply clause places one on the construct and one on the rectum.

Three English 'you's answer to the single אֶתְכֶם, whose scope is distributed across the three coordinated verbs; kept as one discontinuous unit under rules 18 and 25 rather than marking two of them added.
Two judgment calls are recorded in unit notes: 'it' in 'to melt it' is added (no object morpheme), while 'there' in 'lay you there' is kept inside the verb's unit.
